review_method: Independent original-map pixel inspection, complete source and baseline-rendered ring plots, registered overlays, publication imprint and enlarged first-target part and southeast-context views. All 441 ordered positions across four parts and four closed rings were independently compared with the source, decoded geometries and summaries. The embedded GeoPDF affine was independently reopened and all registrations recomputed, including both rotation terms. The retained successful original acquisition receipt was verified against the original bytes. Every selected position falls within an inspected original crop. Complete outlines, orientation, separate neighboring waters, mapped land, water-label typography and material omitted extensions were considered together; neither bounds nor label overlap alone established identity. The production decoder was not independently replayed by this reviewer.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory lake target IDs; repeated map labels do not increase the target count.

findings.follow_up_scope: Before assigning any whole-feature scalar name, resolve the North Moose and South Moose named-water partitions, eastern-arm name assignment and the tiny southern part against appropriately authorized detailed evidence. This is a name-scope hold, not an access failure.
findings.supported_name_scope: North Moose Lake and South Moose Lake are distinct associations within the main selected part, not aliases or a single whole-feature identity. The main part combines distinct North Moose Lake and South Moose Lake associations, which are non-exhaustive. The eastern arm near Davidson Lake has no established exact name assignment. The narrow four-position southern part has no independently established water-name assignment and falls across a mapped land/shoreline area. Shorelines, islands and narrow connections are generalized; exact named-water partitions and complete detailed named-lake extents are unverified. Exact extent and product-name application are not approved.
limits: The main part combines distinct North Moose Lake and South Moose Lake associations, which are non-exhaustive. The eastern arm near Davidson Lake has no established exact name assignment. The narrow four-position southern part has no independently established water-name assignment and falls across a mapped land/shoreline area. Shorelines, islands and narrow connections are generalized; exact named-water partitions and complete detailed named-lake extents are unverified.

Talbot Lake lies in the east-central gap outside the main ring. A small separately labelled Davidson Lake basin lies east of the southeastern arm, with mapped land between the displayed basin and arm; the exact named extent of the selected arm is not established; Mawdesley, Driftwood and Bracken lakes are also separately labelled neighbors.

One retained official Manitoba Geological Survey publication supports the associations. One provincial-government publisher group is represented; underlying hydrographic dataset independence and formal naming-registry authority are unverified.
No Korean form or additional whole-feature alias is certified; registered overlays do not establish surveyed shores or exact name partitions.
